headline: The semis ETF fell another 2.7% (-19.8% on the month) as Marvell's $115bn all-stock Lumentum deal and Apple's memory-cost warning hit AI hardware, while grid (+2.6% on five days) and Vertiv (+12.2%) held up again.
regime: Nasdaq -1.1% and the semis ETF -2.7% on the day, with the semis ETF -19.8% and the Nasdaq -8.4% on the month; VIX is 21.4 (+22% on five days). The 10-year eased to 4.89% but crude is $98.46 (+10.1% on the month), and the midterm elections are today. Software (-17.4% on five days, ServiceNow -33%) and optical (-34.4% on the month) are weakest, while grid is the only segment up on the day and five days. The split between backlog-rich power suppliers and financed or crowded AI hardware continues.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Eaton reported record Q3 with accelerating record orders and backlog and raised organic growth guidance (1031895278ba)
Grid +2.6% and Vertiv-led cooling's best name +12.2% on five days while compute is -11.9% (digest segments)
Bernstein says data-centre political risk is overstated and names Quanta, Eaton, Vertiv, Equinix (cc44df149c90)
Against: grid -14.4% and cooling -18.9% on the month; a momentum fund sold Vertiv (28c224185106)
theses.change_note: +2: Eaton's record orders and raised guidance are fresh company-level confirmation, and grid was the only segment green today.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Fabrinet revenue +51% with data-centre revenue +78% and guidance to $1.6bn (278497a09035)
Western Digital revenue +55% and a 17% dividend rise (c9e5434c538a)
Against: Dell says chip supply is 'a lot closer' to demand and its inventory tripled (1823bdf7bfcb)
Against: compute -24.9% and foundry equipment -30.3% on the month (digest segments)
theses.change_note: -1: Fabrinet confirms demand, but Dell's inventory and the 30% monthly drops say the market sees supply catching up.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Applied Digital's CEO says 800 MW still lacks financing; Nebius and CoreWeave fell 6% (4db672b519c5)
CoreWeave, ASTS and RGTI hit 52-week lows (dbdea76d4895); the bond market signals distress on CoreWeave (511771078b39)
Oracle is raising $20bn of stock and bonds to fund AI spending (5b45ee908598)
Against: Cipher swung to GAAP profit with $16.6bn of contracted revenue (af74089e3bac)
theses.change_note: +2: another financing admission, new lows and a quality gate that again drops all the leveraged names.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Apple says memory prices keep rising into next year, hurting its margins (11590112e625)
Western Digital revenue +55% (c9e5434c538a)
Against: Seagate -30% in a month and Micron -34% off its high (002a16def5d2, dfea31095e8d)
Against: Dell's tripled inventory suggests buyers are stocking ahead of supply easing (1823bdf7bfcb)
theses.change_note: -5: rising prices prove the shortage but also create demand destruction at Apple and Dell; the group fell 6.9% in a day anyway.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Oracle's $20bn equity and bond raise to fund AI expansion (0281d1fb948b)
CPP Investments sees 'bubble-like exuberance' in AI debt (e3efb52151d6)
Against: Mizuho raised its Amazon target on AWS growth (ff6334c990d9)
Against: the group fell 2.2% on the day, least of the AI groups (digest segments)
theses.change_note: Oracle's raise supports the thesis and Amazon's upgrade offsets it.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Semis ETF -19.8% and VIX +38% on the month, with 10-year 4.89% and crude $98 (digest tape)
Marvell-Lumentum deal triggered a plunge in both and a TD Cowen downgrade with the target halved to $175 (d37e4489b821)
Index funds sold NVIDIA and Microsoft on Oct. 30 (bc7b5c398be9)
Against: the 10-year is down 7.3% on the month and Nvidia ticked up after a four-day rout (f1d774e7fa2d)
theses.change_note: +2: another -2.7% semis day and a $115bn all-stock deal punished by both sides; the easing yield limits the move.

compute.note: -5.4% on the day, -24.9% on the month; Marvell -26.7% on five days, only Broadcom holds.

foundry_equipment.note: -30.3% on the month; KLA +2.6% but Teradyne -15.5% on five days; buy only quality.

memory_storage.note: -6.9% on the day; Apple and Dell margin pressure from memory costs.

networking_optical.note: -34.4% on the month; Lumentum -19% on the Marvell deal, though Fabrinet's results were strong.

servers.note: Dell -15.9% on five days with tripled inventory; HPE ranked Zacks #1.

power_nuclear.note: Constellation and NRG slipped; own cash-flow producers only, developers burn cash.

grid_electrical.note: Only green segment; Eaton record orders and raised guidance, MasTec +12.3% on five days.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv +12.2% on five days but less margin of safety; Trane -9.2%.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Financing gaps at Applied Digital and 52-week lows at CoreWeave; fails the cash-flow gate.

hyperscalers.note: Oracle raising $20bn to fund capex; Alphabet -11.9% on five days.

ai_software.note: -17.4% on five days with ServiceNow -33%; Palantir fell despite a beat.

risks: A further semis leg down after the midterms could force selling in the order-book names that have held up.
Memory costs squeezing Apple and Dell margins could cut hardware orders across the chain.
Oil near $98 amid reported US-Iran strikes and a 10-year near 4.9% keep multiples compressed.
Neocloud and Oracle financing stress could delay GPU, power and cooling orders.
Sell-the-news on good prints (Palantir, Apple) means being right on fundamentals can still lose money.
watch: Market reaction to the midterm election results.
AMD earnings and whether Marvell and Lumentum stabilise after the deal.
Primoris (today) and Rigetti (Nov 10) reports for grid backlog and speculative tech sentiment.
Whether the semis ETF breaks below -20% on the month.
Applied Digital and CoreWeave financing news and CoreWeave earnings.
